html:
Maumoon Abdul Gayoom was president of the Maldives from 1978 to 2008, the longest serving leader in Asia at the time. He was born in Male in 1937 and studied Islamic law at Al-Azhar in Cairo.

His years in power brought the tourist boom, schools and clinics on the outer islands, and a much richer country. He survived the coup attempt of 1988 with India's help, and in the 1980s he was among the first leaders to warn the world that rising seas could drown low island nations.

He also jailed critics and won six elections with no rival on the ballot. Protests after a death in custody in 2003 forced reforms. In 2008, in the first multiparty election, he lost to the former prisoner Mohamed Nasheed.
sum: Maumoon Abdul Gayoom was president of the Maldives from 1978 to 2008, the longest serving leader in Asia at the time. He was born in Male in 1937 and studied Islamic law at Al-Azhar in Cairo.
